text:
megan: Heads up — saw a tenant burst in eu-west that dropped ~15% p50 on adjacent slices. Not classic noisy neighbor (CPU/GPU okay) but links to a single rack NIC flapping under microbursts.

sam: ugh, saw the spikes in the routing dashboards. Was it from a dedicated pool or multi-tenant?

megan: Multi-tenant warm pool. The tenant had a sudden series of short-lived allocations (lots of tiny inference jobs).

jia: Were KV cache misses correlated? Could be regen storms causing extra egress.

megan: KV miss rate jumped x4 for the tenant. Also saw sustained 200-300pps on the rack uplink for ~40s bursts.

omar: Can you paste the traceroute or netstat snippet?

megan: here's the capture from the edge proxy logs (filtered):

```
time=2026-03-15T04:12:31Z level=warn component=proxy flow=out pkt_drops=78 conn_queue_len=512
time=2026-03-15T04:12:32Z level=info component=kvcache miss=0.42 tenant=team-alpha
time=2026-03-15T04:12:35Z level=warn component=nic rx_errors=12
```

ellie: rx_errors on NIC typically indicate driver/firmware jitter + saturation. Which hardware?

megan: Rack: r12-3, ToR Broadcom, hosts are A100s with Mellanox 100g NIC. Firmware updated last month.

sam: Hmm. Not firmware regress then. Could be queue hogging from lots of tiny connections. Our default NIC shaping allows big flows but small bursty flows can overflow nic queues.

jia: Proposal: introduce a sandboxed short-lived pool (call it "burst-sandbox") with aggressive per-tenant conn caps and per-socket qlen limits so we absorb microbursts without hitting rack uplink. Thoughts?

omar: Nice. Also add a routing policy that pins sandboxed traffic to spare uplink paths (if available) and marks them lower priority so they back off via ECN.

megan: +1. We should prefer software-level TCP QDISC shaping first (tc) before changing hardware. Quick experiment: reduce fq_codel target and set limits on conntrack for that tenant class.

ops-bot: NOTE: Canary job queued: infra/canaries/burst-sandbox-test -> triggered by megan at 2026-03-15T04:22:00Z

ellie: If we go with sandbox pools we need cost accounting. Dedicated pools are expensive; sandbox must be meta-tagged and costed to tenant when used.

sam: Agreed. Implementation plan:
- short term (hrs): tc + fq_codel tweak on affected ToR, enable ECN marking upstream. (owners: megan, sam)
- mid term (days): add sandbox pool label and routing policy; conn & token bucket caps (owner: jia)
- long term (weeks): automation to migrate noisy tenants automatically into sandbox when metrics exceed thresholds + billing hooks (owner: omar)

jia: I'll sketch the RBAC and policy change. For automation, threshold = >200 conn/s sustained and KV miss > 1.5x baseline for 30s. That should catch this pattern.

megan: I'll run the tc experiment now on r12-3, will report back in ~10m. If it reduces rx_errors we can roll to other racks.

omar: Also capture histograms for p50/p95 pre/post. We need clear SLO delta when sandboxed.

megan: quick update: patched fq_codel on r12-3, initial rx_errors dropped to near zero, tenant p50 recovered to baseline within 60s.

sam: Nice! Can you paste the before/after numbers?

megan: before p50 220ms, p95 980ms; after p50 95ms, p95 320ms. KV miss down to 1.2x.

ellie: Great signal. Proceed with mid-term plan. Jira ticket?

jia: created INFRA-7123 sandbox pool + routing policy, link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-7123

ops-bot: Deployment success: infra/canaries/burst-sandbox-test (run-42) -> all checks passed

megan: I'll monitor overnight, if stable we'll ship a lightweight automation to flag tenants into sandbox next week. Thanks team :thumbsup:
